technique: Sampling-based spot check. The prover commits to the execution trace with a Merkle-tree vector commitment (SHA-256 row-wise hashes). App. I.4 (p.49): 'a soundness error of approximately (eps_sep + eps_tst)', with example targets eps_sep = 0.01 (Alg. 1, p.48) and eps_target = 0.05 (p.49). technique: Activation fingerprint (locality-sensitive hash). The provider takes the top-k (k=128) indices and values of the last hidden state every 32 generated tokens, plus one set for the prompt. It encodes them as a polynomial congruence modulo an injective modulus, with 2-byte coefficients (Sec. 4, p.3; Sec. 5.8, p.7). The validator re-runs one prefill over all tokens with the claimed model. It accepts if the exponent-mismatch count, the mean mantissa diff and the median mantissa diff are under thresholds: bf16 Texp=38, Tmean=10, Tmedian=8; fp32 Texp=8, Tmean=256, Tmedian=128 (Sec. 5.2, p.4). Complexity (App. C, p.12): Newton interpolation O(k^2); Horner evaluation O(k); injective-modulus search O(k) with a worst-case constant of 65,536; modular inverse O(log M). The validator's cost is a full prefill of the model.

trust_assumptions: A trusted validator holds the correct model and a GPU and re-runs the prefill. Thresholds are calibrated for GPU nondeterminism. There is no cryptographic binding of weights.
handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no algebraic check; the validator recomputes the full model, so any architecture works (Llama, Intellect-1 and Gemma-2 were tested).

venue_year: arXiv 2410.22307 (v1 Oct 2024; v3 31 Jan 2026, marked 'Preprint'); also on OpenReview (id OaKEGJLhP9)
technique: Secret-based hidden-state fingerprint. The provider returns the generated text plus processed hidden states of the prompt. A proxy task maps hidden states to a 128-dim label vector: a 4-layer transformer feature extractor g run by the provider, and an MLP head f plus a task-embedding network t run by the user. A labelling network y(x, s), built from a sentence transformer plus MLPs, generates the target label from the prompt and a 48-bit secret s. The verifier accepts if the L2 distance is at most eta. Secrets rotate after M* queries (typically 400-600); the protocol is retrained after N* secrets. Batch hypothesis testing aggregates per-query outcomes.
soundness_error_stated: Statistical, with no strict security guarantee (App. B.1, p.12). Per query: FNR below 5% and FPR below 3% (abstract; Table 2). Batch rule, Theorem B.1 (p.13): Pr(Vbar < tau | honest) <= exp(-2B(p1 - tau)^2) and Pr(Vbar >= tau | dishonest) <= exp(-2B(tau - p0)^2). Theorem 3.1 (p.5): B=30 gives both errors below 10^-5 for per-query rates below 5%. Example (Gaussian approximation, App. B.3): B=30, tau=0.5, Llama-3.1-70B vs Llama-2-7B gives type-I 1.7x10^-49 and type-II 0.0 (p.7, p.14). The secret-guess success rate is 1 - delta, e.g. 0.53% for Llama-2-13B (Table 13, p.20).
trust_assumptions: A trusted platform or third party trains the labelling network and proxy task and manages secrets. The provider must not obtain the user's secret. Adaptive attacks are bounded only empirically: adapter attack (Fig. 4) and secret recovery (below 50% ASR up to 200,000 pairs, Table 3).
handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no computation check; it tests model identity through a learned proxy on hidden states.

venue_year: arXiv 2502.19405v1, 26 Feb 2025 (preprint; Gensyn AI / NYU / a16z crypto research)
technique: Refereed delegation / dispute resolution. The client sends the same program to k >= 2 providers. If outputs differ, a two-phase narrowing over hashed state runs. Phase 1 finds the first diverging training/inference step with multi-level checkpointing: N checkpoint hashes per level, recursing into the diverging interval, without binary search (Alg. 1, p.3; footnote 2, p.4). Phase 2 finds the first diverging operator by comparing the full sequences of AugmentedCGNode hashes, which are Merkle-committed as the checkpoint (Alg. 2, p.5). The referee then resolves by graph-structure check, Merkle membership proof, or re-executing one operator (Sec. 2.3). RepOps provides bitwise-reproducible CUDA operators with a fixed floating-point reduction order.

technique: Optimistic verification with a Merkle-anchored, threshold-guided interactive dispute game. The game recursively partitions the traced PyTorch graph N ways down to a single operator. At the leaf, the operator is judged against IEEE-754 theoretical bounds (deterministic or probabilistic) or against empirical percentile thresholds calibrated across GPUs. The empirical option is adjudicated by a small honest-majority committee vote. Coordination runs on an Ethereum (Holesky testnet) contract.
soundness_error_stated: Empirical plus crypto-economic. With empirical thresholds, ASR is 0.0% for all models even when loosened 3x, with 0% false positives (p.4, Table 2 p.9). With theoretical bounds only, the probabilistic bound allows up to 2.4% ASR on Qwen3-8B (x1) and the deterministic bound up to 12.6% (Qwen3-8B) and 58.6% (BERT-large). ResNet-152 has 0.0% ASR under all bounds. Dispute rounds are ~O(log_N |V|) (Fig. 8 caption, p.13).
trust_assumptions: At least one honest challenger within the challenge window. An honest-majority committee at the leaf when empirical thresholds are used. A smart-contract coordinator. Merkle commitments to weights and topology. Software determinism flags (fixed seeds, deterministic cuBLAS/cuDNN, TF32 off).
handles_nonlinear: Yes. Per-operator tolerance bounds cover arbitrary PyTorch operators running on native FP32 vendor kernels.

system: SLP: Seal, Then Sample (extra: sampled zk proofs)
technique: A hybrid of sampling and SNARKs. The prover commits to the boundary activations of every chunk (2L+3 chunks for L blocks: 47 for TinyLlama, 163 for Llama-2-70B; p.4). Commitments use HyperKZG over BN254 with a Blake3 transcript, and all of them are absorbed before any challenge is drawn. The prover then proves a random subset of candidate chunks plus the input/output anchor chunks. Linear layers use GKR-style sumcheck; nonlinear ones use LogUp-family lookups (p.3). The system is built on a modified deep-prove checkout (Gailly et al., 2026). A packed-batch mode uses a block-diagonal causal mask. The proven object is a fixed-point canonical model.
soundness_error_stated: Per audit, a false manifest is accepted with probability <= q(M,b,s) + eps_backend, where q = C(M-b,s)/C(M,s) (Sec. 3.3, p.4). The 70B run (M=161, s=3, b=1) gives coverage 3/161 = 1.863%. Cumulative detection is 1-(1-p)^k: 37 audits for 50%, 160 for 95% (p.5). With a manifest-only Fiat-Shamir schedule, grinding costs ~12.5 ms per attempt on GPT-2 (p.9), so an externally ordered challenge is required.
trust_assumptions: Binding commitments and a sound backend. All measurements use a locally generated test reference string (insecure against its generator). An authenticated registry/config and an external, unpredictable challenge (beacon) with enforced ordering and unique accepted manifests are required. No zero-knowledge claim is made (p.2).
handles_nonlinear: Yes, via LogUp-family lookup arguments. LayerNorm/RMSNorm gadgets admit an approximation range with explicit error bounds (Sec. 8.2).
weights_public: GPT-2 (Q8_0 GGUF source) and TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0 are public (ungated on HF). Llama-2-70B came from the NousResearch distribution (ungated HF mirror; Llama 2 licence). WikiText-2 is public.

technique: Token-DiFR replays the generated tokens with a trusted reference implementation under a synchronised sampling seed (Gumbel-max sampling) and scores the divergence, e.g. the sampled-token margin. Activation-DiFR sends random orthogonal projections of activations as a k-dimensional fingerprint, logged on J tokens per 32-token window, and compares them by distance. Batch-level classifiers are evaluated by AUC at FPR < 1%.
soundness_error_stated: Statistical (AUC at FPR < 1%), with no cryptographic bound. Token-DiFR detects 4-bit quantisation with AUC > 0.999 within 300 output tokens. Activation-DiFR does so with 2 tokens (abstract; Tables 2-3 are for Qwen3-30B-A3B).
trust_assumptions: A trusted reference implementation re-runs inference. Token-DiFR needs a shared sampling seed; Activation-DiFR needs a shared projection seed.
handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no algebraic check; the reference recomputes the forward pass.

technique: Token-DiFR replays the generated tokens with a trusted reference implementation under a synchronised sampling seed (Gumbel-max sampling) and scores the divergence, e.g. the sampled-token margin. Activation-DiFR sends random orthogonal projections of activations as a k-dimensional fingerprint, logged on J tokens per 32-token window, and compares them by distance. Batch-level classifiers are evaluated by AUC at FPR < 1%.
soundness_error_stated: Statistical (AUC at FPR < 1%), with no cryptographic bound. Token-DiFR detects 4-bit quantisation with AUC > 0.999 within 300 output tokens. Activation-DiFR does so with 2 tokens (abstract; Tables 2-3 are for Qwen3-30B-A3B).
trust_assumptions: A trusted reference implementation re-runs inference. Token-DiFR needs a shared sampling seed; Activation-DiFR needs a shared projection seed.
handles_nonlinear: Not applicable. There is no algebraic check; the reference recomputes the forward pass.

technique: NOT Freivalds. It is an interactive proof: Thaler's (CRYPTO'13) sum-check IP for matrix multiplication plus a new sum-check IP for quadratic activations, in a GKR-style layer-by-layer reduction over F_p (multilinear extensions), batched over b inputs. Stated complexity (Sec 3.1-3.2, pp.5-6): matmul layer i prover O(n_i(n_{i-1}+b)), verifier O(n_i n_{i-1}), 4 log(n_i) field elements exchanged; quadratic-activation layer prover O(b n_i), verifier O(log(b n_i)), 5 log(b n_i) field elements.
soundness_error_stated: Lemma 3.1 (p.6): eps = 3b * sum_{i=0}^{L} n_i / p. Paper: 'with p = 2^61 - 1 the soundness error < 1/2^30 for practical network parameters and batch sizes'. Sec 4.3: in all settings eps < 1/2^30. This is statistical (information-theoretic) soundness for an interactive protocol.
trust_assumptions: No trusted hardware. Interactive public-coin IP with the client as verifier. Weights are known to both parties, and the verifier evaluates the weight MLE locally. There are no commitments and no model privacy. Only arithmetic-circuit networks (quadratic activations) are supported.

ReLU, sigmoid and softmax are allowed only in the final output layer, where the prover sends z_{L-1} and the client computes the output activation itself. Max pooling and stochastic pooling are not supported at all.

technique: An Intel SGX TEE outsources every linear layer (FC, conv, depthwise/pointwise conv) to an untrusted co-located GPU and checks each result with Freivalds' algorithm over Z_p. The paper uses three variants: (a) on-the-fly Freivalds, (b) batched Freivalds, and (c) Freivalds with preprocessing, where the secret s and s~ = W s are precomputed so each check costs |x|+|y| multiplications. Privacy comes from additive stream-cipher blinding with precomputed unblinding factors. Complexity: Table 2 (p.6), e.g. FC batched verification B(|x|+|y|)+cost_f and with preprocessing B(|x|+|y|). A plain Freivalds check costs 3n^2 multiplications (Lemma 2.1, p.4).
soundness_error_stated: Theorem 3.2 (p.6): t-integrity with t = n/|S|^k - negl(lambda) for an n-layer DNN and k Freivalds repetitions per layer. Implementation (Sec 4.1, p.7): p = 2^24 - 3, k = 2, S = [-2^19, 2^19], '40 bits of statistical soundness per layer'. For a 50-layer DNN, the chance of fooling the TEE is 'less than 1 in 22 billion'.
trust_assumptions: The TEE (Intel SGX enclave) is trusted: it is the verifier, holds the model and the secret Freivalds randomness (designated verifier, s reused across layers), and attests to remote clients. The GPU/host is untrusted. Privacy relies on a secure PRNG (AES-CTR/GCM). The paper notes SGX side-channel caveats. Offline preprocessing is needed for the preproc/privacy modes.
handles_nonlinear: Non-linearities (ReLU, pooling, residual merges) are computed directly inside the trusted enclave and are not cryptographically verified. ResNets are handled by verifying the linear layers in both residual paths and computing the activation in the TEE.
weights_public: Pretrained VGG16, MobileNet and ResNet50 are the public Keras ImageNet weights (paper Appendix E; downloadable without an account). ResNet-18/34/101/152 throughput was measured on untrained models. Accuracy is measured on the ImageNet validation set, which requires registration on image-net.org. The repo README warns it is a proof-of-concept for performance testing only and says nothing about weight sourcing.

Privacy comes from additive stream-cipher blinding with precomputed unblinding factors. Complexity: Table 2 (p.6), e.g. FC batched verification B(|x|+|y|)+cost_f and with preprocessing B(|x|+|y|). A plain Freivalds check costs 3n^2 multiplications (Lemma 2.1, p.4).
soundness_error_stated: Theorem 3.2 (p.6): t-integrity with t = n/|S|^k - negl(lambda) for an n-layer DNN and k Freivalds repetitions per layer. Implementation (Sec 4.1, p.7): p = 2^24 - 3, k = 2, S = [-2^19, 2^19], '40 bits of statistical soundness per layer'. For a 50-layer DNN, the chance of fooling the TEE is 'less than 1 in 22 billion'.
trust_assumptions: The TEE (Intel SGX enclave) is trusted: it is the verifier, holds the model and the secret Freivalds randomness (designated verifier, s reused across layers), and attests to remote clients. The GPU/host is untrusted. Privacy relies on a secure PRNG (AES-CTR/GCM). The paper notes SGX side-channel caveats. Offline preprocessing is needed for the preproc/privacy modes.
handles_nonlinear: Non-linearities (ReLU, pooling, residual merges) are computed directly inside the trusted enclave and are not cryptographically verified. ResNets are handled by verifying the linear layers in both residual paths and computing the activation in the TEE.
weights_public: Pretrained VGG16, MobileNet and ResNet50 are the public Keras ImageNet weights (paper Appendix E; downloadable without an account). ResNet-18/34/101/152 throughput was measured on untrained models. Accuracy is measured on the ImageNet validation set, which requires registration on image-net.org. The repo README warns it is a proof-of-concept for performance testing only and says nothing about weight sourcing.

technique: Sparse Freivalds combined with a linear error-correcting code (RAA codes, rate 1/8, target relative distance 1/2). Transparent preprocessing Q = G^T M. The client samples a t-sparse challenge e and checks (e^T Q)x = e^T(G^T y). Batch verification (Protocol 2) delegates the stacked projections Q_b^T e to the server and checks them with a second coded check. Privacy uses dual-LPN pseudorandom masks x' = G_x e_x with a preprocessed P = M G_x. Complexity: client online O(N + l*t*n) per MVM (Table 1, p.8), O_kappa(m+n) overall. Preprocessing O(mn). Batch client O(BN + B l(n+t) + l' t' B n + l l'(Bn + t t')) (pp.8-9). In the base protocol the honest server performs only the ordinary MVM. Batch verification adds one round and O(B l t n) server field operations, returning B l n field elements (p.9).
soundness_error_stated: Information-theoretic. Each repetition accepts a wrong y with probability <= (1-delta)^t + 1/(|F|-1) (Lemma 5.1, p.7). With l repetitions the soundness error is <= 2^-kappa (Theorem 5.2, pp.7-8), plus p_fail of the sampled code (Remark 5.3, p.8). Batch verification: eps^l + (eps')^l' (Theorem 5.4, p.8). Parameters: kappa = 40 (statistical), lambda = 128 (computational, privacy); BabyBear field q = 15*2^27 + 1; t_y = 31, l = 2; t_x = 160..154 for n = 2^10..2^14.
trust_assumptions: No TEE and no trusted setup. The model is public; preprocessing is transparent, and anyone can check Q. Soundness is information-theoretic against an unbounded server. Input privacy is computational under dual-LPN (RAA codes assumed 'plausibly dual-LPN-friendly'). The protocol is interactive (182 rounds in standard/boost mode, 1 round in verification-only mode).
handles_nonlinear: Nonlinear operations are not verified cryptographically. The client evaluates them locally, which the paper says is <1% of inference time (p.2). In verification-only mode the server runs the whole model and the client replays the nonlinear operations locally from the returned y_j to reconstruct each x_j before batch-checking M_j x_j = y_j.

trust_assumptions: No TEE and no trusted setup. The model is public; preprocessing is transparent, and anyone can check Q. Soundness is information-theoretic against an unbounded server. Input privacy is computational under dual-LPN (RAA codes assumed 'plausibly dual-LPN-friendly'). The protocol is interactive (182 rounds in standard/boost mode, 1 round in verification-only mode).
handles_nonlinear: Nonlinear operations are not verified cryptographically. The client evaluates them locally, which the paper says is <1% of inference time (p.2). The client samples a t-sparse challenge e and checks (e^T Q)x = e^T(G^T y). Batch verification (Protocol 2) delegates the stacked projections Q_b^T e to the server and checks them with a second coded check. Privacy uses dual-LPN pseudorandom masks x' = G_x e_x with a preprocessed P = M G_x. Complexity: client online O(N + l*t*n) per MVM (Table 1, p.8), O_kappa(m+n) overall. Preprocessing O(mn). Batch client O(BN + B l(n+t) + l' t' B n + l l'(Bn + t t')) (pp.8-9). In the base protocol the honest server performs only the ordinary MVM. Batch verification adds one round and O(B l t n) server field operations, returning B l n field elements (p.9).
soundness_error_stated: Information-theoretic. Each repetition accepts a wrong y with probability <= (1-delta)^t + 1/(|F|-1) (Lemma 5.1, p.7). With l repetitions the soundness error is <= 2^-kappa (Theorem 5.2, pp.7-8), plus p_fail of the sampled code (Remark 5.3, p.8). Batch verification: eps^l + (eps')^l' (Theorem 5.4, p.8). Parameters: kappa = 40 (statistical), lambda = 128 (computational, privacy); BabyBear field q = 15*2^27 + 1; t_y = 31, l = 2; t_x = 160..154 for n = 2^10..2^14.
trust_assumptions: No TEE and no trusted setup. The model is public; preprocessing is transparent, and anyone can check Q. Soundness is information-theoretic against an unbounded server. Input privacy is computational under dual-LPN (RAA codes assumed 'plausibly dual-LPN-friendly'). The protocol is interactive (182 rounds in standard/boost mode, 1 round in verification-only mode).
handles_nonlinear: Nonlinear operations are not verified cryptographically. The client evaluates them locally, which the paper says is <1% of inference time (p.2). technique: A commit-and-prove SNARK for a single k x k product AB = C. It combines Freivalds' check (structured challenge r = (1, r, ..., r^{k-1})) with proximity testing over a linear code (Reed-Solomon, rate 1/2). The prover commits to row-wise encoded A, B, C (Pedersen leaves in a Merkle tree) and to encoded intermediates x = rA, y = xB, z = rC. The Groth16 CP-SNARK then checks only t sampled encoded-column fold equations and the RS code-consistency of x, y, z. Merkle openings and QA-NIZK CP-Link bind the in-circuit values to the commitments. Complexity (Table 1, p.9): circuit O(tk + E_code) constraints, linear in k for fixed t. Prover O(3nk) group ops + O(n) hashes for the ABC commit and O(k^2) field ops for the intermediates. Verifier E^V_snark + O(t log n) hashes + E^V_link (O(t) pairing terms). Parameters: t = 128, RS rate 1/2.

system: ZKML (Chen, Waiwitlikhit, Stoica, Kang) [extra: Freivalds-based matmul inside halo2; benchmarks ResNet-18]
technique: An optimizing compiler from TFLite to halo2 ZK-SNARK circuits, with gadget selection and layout optimisation. For linear layers (FC, conv, batched matmul) it can compute B outside the circuit and check B r = W A r with Freivalds' algorithm (O(n^2) instead of O(n^3)). The random r is generated after the matrices and results are committed (Sec 6, p.8). The paper does not say per benchmark whether the Freivalds gadget was used. The backends are KZG or IPA polynomial commitments.
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. The paper says ZKML inherits the zero-knowledge, completeness and knowledge-soundness properties of halo2 (Sec 4.3, p.5). Assumptions depend on the KZG or IPA backend.
trust_assumptions: KZG needs a universal trusted setup; the paper uses the Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 with over 75 participants. IPA is transparent but has larger proofs and slower verification. Non-interactive (Fiat-Shamir). The verifier needs the model configuration and verifying key but not the weights (p.10).
handles_nonlinear: Yes, fully in-circuit. ReLU and other pointwise nonlinearities use lookup-table gadgets (e.g., ReLU with 2 cells via a lookup table vs b+2 cells by bit decomposition). Softmax (max + scaled exp + variable division), exp and division have dedicated gadgets. All nonlinearities are proved.
weights_public: The repo ships an MNIST model (examples/mnist/model.tflite and model.msgpack) and a MobileNet v2 (1.0, 224) TFLite (testing/circuits/v2_1.0_224.tflite, about 14 MB, plus a truncated variant). It also has config/input msgpack files for GPT-2, CLIP and Twitter, which are too small to contain the full weights. There are no ResNet-18 or VGG16 CIFAR-10 models, and the paper does not say the ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 weights were released. CIFAR-10 is public. ImageNet data requires registration.
verifier_corrections: Every value in Tables 5, 6, 7, 8, 9 and 10, the instance-to-model mapping (r6i.8xlarge / 16xlarge / 32xlarge) and the security/Freivalds text (Sec 4.3 p.5, Sec 6 p.8) matches the EuroSys'24 PDF. LAMP (p.2) does cite zkML as using 'Freivalds' randomized checks'. || weights_public was wrong. The repo does not ship only an MNIST model. Per the GitHub tree API it contains examples/mnist/model.tflite and model.msgpack, a MobileNet v2 (1.0, 224) TFLite at testing/circuits/v2_1.0_224.tflite (about 14 MB), a truncated variant at examples/v2_1.0_224_truncated/, and config/input msgpack files for GPT-2, CLIP and Twitter (100-260 kB each, too small to hold the full weights). It has no ResNet-18 or VGG16 CIFAR-10 models. || Notes, Table 9 explanation: the paper says only that 'to estimate the cost of proving for prior work, we match the hardware setup used in the prior work as closely as possible'. It never attributes the VGG-16 584.1 s (vs 637.14 s in Table 6) to hardware. Table 9's ResNet-18 prove time (52.9 s) is identical to Table 6, so the cause of the difference is not established. || The paper says Freivalds 'can' be used for linear layers (Sec 6). It does not say, per benchmark, whether the reported runs used the Freivalds gadget.
hardware: AWS r6i.8xlarge (32 vCPU threads, 256 GB RAM)

For linear layers (FC, conv, batched matmul) it can compute B outside the circuit and check B r = W A r with Freivalds' algorithm (O(n^2) instead of O(n^3)). The random r is generated after the matrices and results are committed (Sec 6, p.8). The paper does not say per benchmark whether the Freivalds gadget was used. The backends are KZG or IPA polynomial commitments.
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. The paper says ZKML inherits the zero-knowledge, completeness and knowledge-soundness properties of halo2 (Sec 4.3, p.5). Assumptions depend on the KZG or IPA backend.
trust_assumptions: KZG needs a universal trusted setup; the paper uses the Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 with over 75 participants. IPA is transparent but has larger proofs and slower verification. Non-interactive (Fiat-Shamir). The verifier needs the model configuration and verifying key but not the weights (p.10).
handles_nonlinear: Yes, fully in-circuit. ReLU and other pointwise nonlinearities use lookup-table gadgets (e.g., ReLU with 2 cells via a lookup table vs b+2 cells by bit decomposition). Softmax (max + scaled exp + variable division), exp and division have dedicated gadgets. All nonlinearities are proved.
weights_public: The repo ships an MNIST model (examples/mnist/model.tflite and model.msgpack) and a MobileNet v2 (1.0, 224) TFLite (testing/circuits/v2_1.0_224.tflite, about 14 MB, plus a truncated variant). It also has config/input msgpack files for GPT-2, CLIP and Twitter, which are too small to contain the full weights. There are no ResNet-18 or VGG16 CIFAR-10 models, and the paper does not say the ResNet-18 CIFAR-10 weights were released. CIFAR-10 is public. ImageNet data requires registration.

system: TwinShield [extra: random-linear-combination (hash-row) integrity for TEE+GPU; benchmarks LLaMA-7B]
venue_year: arXiv 2507.03278v2 (2025); also an OpenReview submission titled 'TwinShield: Secure Foundation Model Execution by Unifying TEEs and Crypto-protected Accelerators'
technique: An SGX TEE offloads linear layers, attention matmuls (OutAttnMult) and the exponentiations of SoftMax (OutSoftMax) to an untrusted GPU. Integrity uses 'U-Verify': the TEE samples a secret random vector h and appends the hash row hash_A = h*A to A. The GPU computes the augmented product, and the TEE checks h*C = hash_A*B, a Freivalds-style check with 2 instead of 3 vector-matrix products. Softmax exponentiation is checked multiplicatively with secret random integer coefficients a_i: prod(e^{x_i})^{a_i} = e^{hash_X}. Stated complexity (Sec V, pp.8-9): the TEE hash costs n*m multiplications, the GPU (m+1)*n*p, and TEE verification m*p. Softmax verification needs up to n(a_max - 1) + n multiplications. Quantization follows Slalom/DarKnight.
soundness_error_stated: Stated as 'security levels', not a formal soundness theorem. U-Verify for OutSoftMax: attack success rate limited to 1/(n*2^d), security level log(n*2^d), raised with OutSoftMax masking to log(n*2^d*d^n) (p.8). OutAttnMult privacy level log(d*(2m)!), where d is the field size, e.g. 'approximately 13,471 bits' for BERT (p.6). Field Z_p with p = 2^24 - 3.
trust_assumptions: Trusted Intel SGX enclave (verifier; holds the secret hash vectors, coefficients and masks). The GPU/accelerator is untrusted. Designated-verifier: the secrets must stay hidden from the GPU. One-time use of scalars/masks prevents replay.
handles_nonlinear: SoftMax exponentiation is outsourced and verified with the U-Verify random-coefficient product check (secret coefficients); SoftMax additions and divisions stay in the TEE. LayerNorm, GeLU and ReLU stay inside the TEE and are trusted, not verified (<5% of execution time per the paper).
weights_public: The paper says it 'acquired a pre-trained, quantized 8-bit LLaMA model from HuggingFace' without naming the repo. Original LLaMA-7B weights were released by Meta on request, so they are gated. ViT, BERT and CLIP come from Keras. ImageNet needs registration; SST-2 and WikiText are public.
verifier_corrections: Every value in Tables I-VI, the hardware, the model configurations, quantization (l = 8, p = 2^24 - 3), the complexity and the security-level text matches arXiv 2507.03278v2 (v1 4 Jul 2025, v2 13 Jul 2025). || Notes, Fig. 8: the paper says U-Verify gives 'an approximate 33% reduction in latency' versus Freivalds. That is 33% lower latency, not '33% faster'. The Fig. 8 x-axis covers matrix dimensions 256-2048, and no per-point values are labelled. || Notes, Fig. 7: the text says dimension 256 -> 1024 (OutAttnMult 3x -> 11x; OutSoftMax 5x -> 12x), but the plot's x-axis is labelled 'Token Number' 64/128/256. The bar labels read OutAttnMult 3/7/11x (w/o verification 7/18/39x) and OutSoftMax 5/8/12x (12/20/36x). The text and axis disagree inside the paper. || handles_nonlinear: only the exponentiations of SoftMax are outsourced and verified. Its additions and divisions stay in the TEE (Sec IV, p.5). Normalization and activation functions stay in the TEE and account for <5% of execution time. || The OpenReview version (forum nCJF1CDapQ, titled 'TwinShield: Secure Foundation Model Execution by Unifying TEEs and Crypto-protected Accelerators') exists. Its content could not be opened (bot-verification wall), so any numeric differences from arXiv v2 are unchecked. A search-engine summary suggests different headline speedups (3.3x-5.1x vs 4.0x-6.1x); all catalogue numbers are from arXiv v2 only.

system: VeriAttn (CTGA) [extra: Gaussian-variant Freivalds for LLM attention in TEE+GPU; compares against zkLLM]
technique: TEE-shielded partitioning (Intel TDX) that offloads both the linear and the non-linear attention steps to an untrusted GPU. GVFAVeriMM uses the Gaussian variant of Freivalds (secret Gaussian vector w_G, tolerance eps calibrated on honest FP16 GPU runs) to check value aggregation. LPVeriExp uses a log-product random-integer-coefficient check for the softmax exponentiation. Two-level prefill pipelining and TEE-GPU collaborative decoding when the KV cache exceeds GPU memory. Stated verification complexity: prefill O(L^2 + L d_h) instead of O(L^2 d_h); decoding O(t + d_h) per step with an incrementally maintained projection.
soundness_error_stated: Statistical and tolerance-based. Lemma 1: Pr[||(C-AB)w_G||_inf <= eps | C != AB] <= 2*Phi(eps/sigma) - 1 per repetition, (2*Phi(eps/sigma) - 1)^tau over tau repetitions. Lemma 2 (LPVeriExp): Pr[FA_r] <= 1{n_err >= 2}/N_a + (2*Phi(eps'/sigma') - 1)^(tau_g*tau_a). Deviations within the tolerance budget are accepted by design. The experiments use 10 repetitions with tolerance set to 2x the largest clean residual. Empirically 1,000/1,000 injected faults were detected with 0/1,000 false rejections.
trust_assumptions: A trusted Intel TDX CPU TEE acts as verifier and keeps the Gaussian vectors and coefficients secret from the GPU (designated verifier). The GPU is untrusted. Accepted outputs may deviate within the calibrated numerical budget. The paper does not address confidentiality, and side-channel and DoS attacks are out of scope.
handles_nonlinear: Exponentiation in softmax is verified with LPVeriExp (log-product residual with tolerance eps'). Other components (projection and feed-forward layers) follow TSDP, i.e. linear parts offloaded and verified, non-linear parts in the TEE. The whole scheme is tolerance-based floating point, not exact field arithmetic.

technique: GKR/sumcheck interactive proof, made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir in the random oracle model. New linear-time sumcheck for FFT: prover O(M+N), proof and verifier O(log N). 2-D convolution is proven as FFT -> Hadamard product -> IFFT (three sumchecks): prover O(n^2), proof O(log n), or O(log^2 n) proof and verifier in the variant with delegated verifier computation. FC layers use Thaler's matrix-multiplication sumcheck [41]. Generalised GKR gates take inputs from any layer. Weights and auxiliary witness are committed with the Hyrax/Spartan polynomial commitment [39,44] on BLS12-381 (prover O(N), proof and verifier O(sqrt N)).
soundness_error_stated: GKR soundness O(d log|C|/|F|) (Theorem A.1, p.15, citing Libra [48]), where d is circuit depth. The field comes from Curve BLS12-381, which 'offers 128-bits of security' (p.11). Fiat-Shamir 'only incurs a negligible soundness loss' (p.11). The polynomial commitment relies on discrete log. No concrete numeric soundness error is given for the full system.
trust_assumptions: Transparent: no trusted setup or CRS (the paper contrasts this with the tens-of-GB CRSs of vCNN/ZEN). Discrete-log assumption for the polynomial commitment; random oracle for Fiat-Shamir. The ZK variant is described but its 'formal protocol and the proof' are omitted. The code README says 'Currently this version doesn't add complete zero-knowledge property.'
handles_nonlinear: ReLU: a negative x is encoded as p-|x|. The prover supplies the bit decomposition (b_0..b_{Q-1}) of |x| plus a sign bit b_Q (0 negative, 1 positive). The circuit checks that the bits are binary and recompose correctly, then outputs b_Q times the top Q' bits (truncation). Max pooling is fused with ReLU: the prover supplies x_max, each x_max - x_j is bit-decomposed (Q bits, no sign bit), the circuit checks x_max * prod_j(x_max - x_j) = 0, and x_max's own bits are validated. Compared with ReLU alone, that is one extra bit decomposition. Average pooling is supported. Quantisation rescaling by 2^-E uses bit decomposition and shift.

handles_nonlinear: ReLU: a negative x is encoded as p-|x|. The prover supplies the bit decomposition (b_0..b_{Q-1}) of |x| plus a sign bit b_Q (0 negative, 1 positive). The circuit checks that the bits are binary and recompose correctly, then outputs b_Q times the top Q' bits (truncation). Max pooling is fused with ReLU: the prover supplies x_max, each x_max - x_j is bit-decomposed (Q bits, no sign bit), the circuit checks x_max * prod_j(x_max - x_j) = 0, and x_max's own bits are validated. Compared with ReLU alone, that is one extra bit decomposition. Average pooling is supported. Quantisation rescaling by 2^-E uses bit decomposition and shift.

technique: Pairing-based zk-SNARK in the Groth16 style. Convolutions are encoded as a Quadratic Polynomial Program (QPP, polynomial-valued wires); ReLU and pooling go through a QAP. The two are linked with commit-and-prove SNARKs (CP-SNARKs) and Pedersen vector commitments. Convolution proving complexity drops from O(ln) to O(l+n) (l = kernel size, n = data size). The proof is 9 group elements (constant size; 2803 bits in Table II).
soundness_error_stated: 'computational knowledge soundness against adversaries that only use a polynomial number of generic bilinear group operations' (Theorems 1-3). No numeric error or security level is stated.
trust_assumptions: Trusted setup (CRS with simulation trapdoor), generic bilinear group model. CRS sizes are very large (e.g. 83 GB for VGG16, 420 GB for VGG16wFC).
handles_nonlinear: ReLU and pooling are encoded in a QAP arithmetic circuit using bitwise operations, so cost grows with the quantisation bit depth. Real-model experiments use average pooling instead of max pooling because it needs a smaller circuit.
weights_public: The code is a libsnark-based repo (MIT; cited by zkCNN as the vCNN implementation). No trained weights or datasets are included. The paper states no dataset for the Table II real-model runs, only MNIST for the small CNNs. For AlexNet and VGG16 the full-scale numbers are estimates, not measurements.

venue_year: IEEE Transactions on Information Forensics and Security, vol. 18, 2023, pp. 2218-2233 (arXiv 2201.09186)
technique: The CNN is split into a private PriorNet, which the model developer evaluates on HE-encrypted test data (Microsoft SEAL; dc=4096, q=2^109, t=1032193), and a public LaterNet. Correctness is proven with Groth16 zk-SNARKs (libsnark). Convolution and FC are expressed as a single matrix multiplication via a one-degree Quadratic Matrix Program (QMP); ReLU and pooling use QAP circuits. Layers are glued with LegoSNARK-style commit-and-prove, and proofs from multiple testers are aggregated. The paper's Table I gives proving complexity O(Mn^2 · Mn^2), versus O(M·Mn^2·(n^2+m^2)) for vCNN and zkCNN.
soundness_error_stated: Partly quantified. For each PriorNet layer, the random-point polynomial identity check fails with probability dc/q = 4096/2^109, with the point k from a random-oracle HASH (Sec. VI, p.13). The rest relies on the knowledge soundness of the commit-and-prove zk-SNARKs (Groth16/LegoSNARK-based), which is not quantified numerically. Privacy relies on semantic security of the leveled FHE.
trust_assumptions: Trusted setup (Groth16 CRS, very large for QMP: up to 16,927,629,296 KB as reported in Table V), pairing assumptions, random oracle for HASH, FHE semantic security.
handles_nonlinear: ReLU and pooling are QAP-based: 'a ReLU operation needs 20 constraints and an average pooling operation needs 144 constraints'. The circuits use average pooling; the paper also mentions expressing max pooling as QAP.
weights_public: Code is public (libsnark + SEAL; no license file shown on GitHub). The repo contains FHE-LeNet/src/Lenet.h5 (LeNet weights). MNIST and CIFAR-10 are public without an account.

technique: Interactive, designated-verifier ZK based on subfield VOLE (LPN-based sVOLE, Quicksilver [YSWW21]) over F_p with p = 2^61 - 1. It adds efficient arithmetic-to-Boolean conversions (zk-edaBits), conversions from publicly committed to authenticated values (C2A, via a PRF in a Boolean circuit and a Merkle-tree commitment), and fixed-point/floating-point conversions. The matrix-multiplication proof generalises Freivalds' algorithm: an n x n matmul costs n private multiplications instead of n^3, using random vectors u, v over an extension field F_{q^k} and a CheckZero step. It is integrated into the Rosetta (TensorFlow) framework.
soundness_error_stated: 'computational security parameter λ = 128 and statistical security parameter ρ ≥ 40' (p.22). The MatMul protocol has 'soundness error 3/q^k' (Theorem 5, p.18). The edaBits check reaches 'at least 40-bit statistical security' for N = 10^6 (B = 3, c = 2) (p.12). The field is F_p with p = 2^61 - 1.
trust_assumptions: No trusted setup. Interactive: prover and verifier must both be online, and proofs are designated-verifier ('can only prove to one verifier at a time'). sVOLE rests on LPN-style assumptions; hash/PRF for commitments.
handles_nonlinear: ReLU, max pooling, sigmoid, SoftMax and batch normalisation use arithmetic-Boolean conversions (edaBits) and Boolean circuits. IEEE-754 single-precision float circuits (from EMP) with Fix2Float/Float2Fix conversions. Fixed-point encoding uses a 30-bit range with s = 16 fractional bits.
code_url: https://github.com/emp-toolkit/emp-zk (Apache-2.0; its README names Wolverine, Quicksilver and Mystique; F_p = 2^61-1 arithmetic, edaBit conversion bridge, matmul example). The paper cites Rosetta (https://github.com/LatticeX-Foundation/Rosetta) as the host framework; public availability of the ML integration code was not verified.
weights_public: The authors trained LeNet-5, ResNet-50 and ResNet-101 on CIFAR-10; no weight release was found. CIFAR-10 is public without an account.
verifier_corrections: The paper contradicts itself on ResNet-101. The abstract says 28 minutes for 'an inference on a private image using a committed (private) ResNet-101', but Table 4's 'ZK for genuine inference' row (28 m) is defined on p.25 as private-but-committed model with public input. Both readings are recorded; the row stays labelled public input. || LeNet-5 fidelity (99.9% of l2-norm differences below 0.006) is on p.24, not in Table 3. || All Table 2, 3 and 4 numbers, the hardware (2x m5.2xlarge, 32 GB, 'all CPU resources', 12 GB for ResNet-101), lambda = 128 / rho >= 40, the 3/q^k MatMul soundness (Theorem 5, p.18), 40-bit edaBits security (p.12), p = 2^61-1 with 30-bit / s = 16 fixed point (p.19), 62000 / 23.5M / 42.5M params, model sizes and conversion times were confirmed. technique: Optimising framework for zkSNARK NN inference, benchmarked against and built on arkworks (Groth16, cited for 192-byte proofs). It keeps tensor and privacy type information to reduce R1CS work. The ZENO circuit IR makes a dot product O(n) instead of O(n^2) computation, and this extends to FC, conv and pool. 'Knit encoding' packs 8-bit values into 254-bit field elements when only one side (weights or features) is private. It adds a workload-specialised parallel scheduler, constraint-system sharing across a batch of images, and zkSNARK-aware fusion of injective layers (e.g. BN/scale) into conv/FC.
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. It inherits zkSNARK (Groth16 via arkworks) security. The field is '≈2^254 in case of BLS12-381' (p.2), and the text refers to 254-bit finite fields.
trust_assumptions: Groth16-style per-circuit trusted setup (arkworks backend).
handles_nonlinear: ReLU via comparison: the 'circuit first decomposes an integer into n(=254) bits and checks whether the first bit equals zero' (p.4); 'relu requires expensive comparison operator with hundreds of constraints' (p.10), so it is not fused. Average pooling is a dot product with a ones vector. Injective layers such as batch normalisation are fused into the preceding linear layers.

technique: Optimising compiler from ML models (tflite) to halo2 (Plonkish) circuits. A cost-model optimizer chooses among gadget implementations and physical layouts (columns and rows), using fixed-point arithmetic with lookup-table gadgets. Two backends: KZG (universal trusted setup) and IPA (transparent).
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. It 'inherits all security properties of halo2, including zero-knowledge, completeness, and knowledge soundness'.
trust_assumptions: KZG: one-time universal trusted setup (Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 'with over 75 participants'). IPA: transparent, but with larger proofs and slower verification.
handles_nonlinear: Fixed-point with a ZKML-chosen scale factor. Pointwise non-linearities other than ReLU (ELU, sigmoid, exp, tanh) use lookup tables. ReLU can be done by bit decomposition (no lookups, b+2 cells, the zkCNN approach) or by a 2-cell lookup into an (x, ReLU(x)) table; ZKML's layout uses the lookup, and the optimizer picks gadgets. Max uses (c-a)(c-b)=0 plus two range lookups. Softmax uses exp lookups after subtracting the max.
weights_public: Code is public (Apache-2.0). The examples/ folder contains mnist, nlp, train_graph, twitter and v2_1.0_224_truncated (MobileNet v2). No ResNet-18 or VGG16 CIFAR-10 model files were seen in examples/. CIFAR-10 is public. ImageNet download requires registration, but MobileNet v2 weights are public (TF). The distilled GPT-2 is public on Hugging Face.
verifier_corrections: handles_nonlinear was wrong. ZKML does not say its ReLU avoids lookups. Sec. 3 (p.3) contrasts prior-work ReLU by bit decomposition (no lookups, b+2 cells, citing zkCNN) with a 2-cell lookup table (x, f(x)) of at least 2^b rows. ZKML's ReLU layout (p.7) uses a lookup table, and the optimizer chooses among gadget implementations. Max uses a polynomial constraint plus two range lookups; softmax uses exp lookups with a max-subtraction trick. || The claim that Table 9's VGG-16 584.1 s comes from hardware matching is not supported. The paper does not explain why Table 9 differs from Table 6 (VGG-16: 584.1 s vs 637.14 s, 16 ms vs 9.62 ms). ResNet-18 is 52.9 s in both. Table 9's ResNet-18 proof size of 15.3 kB also disagrees with Table 6's 15744 bytes. Recorded as printed. || Fixed-configuration ablation numbers (74.8 s, 1474.0 s, 2407.8 s) come from Table 10, p.12, not Tables 6/8. || Filled verified params from Table 5 (p.10): GPT-2 81.3M params (188.9M flops); Diffusion 19.5M (22.9B flops); Twitter 48.1M (96.2M flops); DLRM 764.3K (1.9M flops). || The examples/ folder also contains train_graph. License is Apache-2.0 (GitHub API). || All Table 6, 7 and 8 numbers, the hardware per model, and the halo2 security and PSE ceremony (2^28, over 75 participants) quotes were confirmed.
other_costs: fixed-config ablation 74.8 s (Table 10, p.12)

system: Kang et al. halo2 DNN (extra: benchmarks MobileNet v2 on ImageNet)
technique: halo2 zk-SNARK: Plonkish arithmetization, a polynomial IOP made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir, and the inner product argument of Bowe et al. 2019. Custom gates and lookup tables handle int8-quantised TF-Lite/TF-Slim DNNs. Evaluated in the hidden-model, hidden-input setting.
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. Cells lie in 'a 254-bit prime field'. Fiat-Shamir heuristic.
trust_assumptions: Not discussed in the paper. It uses halo2 with the Bowe et al. inner product argument, which is transparent by design (our inference). The reported 'setup time' is once-per-architecture key generation, independent of the weights. No numeric security level is stated.
handles_nonlinear: Batch norm is fused into the convolutions. Scale-factor division plus clipped ReLU uses ClipAndScale(c) = clip(floor(c·a/b), 0, 255): a custom gate for the division by a fixed b, then a lookup into table T = {(c, ClipAndScale(c))} shared across layers. Softmax is avoided by returning logits.
weights_public: MobileNet v2 weights come from TensorFlow Slim (public). ImageNet requires registration to download. The paper gives no code URL; the later ZKML repo (uiuc-kang-lab/zkml) is by the same group.
verifier_corrections: The nonlinearity is not 'ReLU6'. The paper defines ClipAndScale(c) = clip(floor(c·a/b), 0, 255), a clipped ReLU plus rescale in the uint8 domain. technique: Compiler from PyTorch/ONNX to circuits for the Expander GKR prover. It has a ZKP preprocessor that inserts auxiliary nodes (e.g. division remainders) into the DAG. ZKP-friendly symmetric per-tensor static integer quantisation shrinks bit widths to fit small fields such as M61. Hierarchical optimisation works at model, operation and circuit level (parallel circuits, lookups).

trust_assumptions: Expander GKR prover. The paper does not state trusted-setup or commitment details.
handles_nonlinear: Integer quantisation. Piecewise lookup tables with temporary bit-width adjustment for the softmax exponent and the RMSNorm square root; auxiliary nodes for remainders in division.
code_url: The Expander prover is open source (ref [7], https://github.com/PolyhedraZK/Expander). The paper does not state whether the zkPyTorch compiler code is available.
weights_public: CIFAR-10 is public. Llama-3-8B is gated (requires accepting Meta's licence on Hugging Face). The paper does not mention releasing the authors' quantised VGG-16/ResNet weights.
verifier_corrections: The Llama-3 99.32% cosine similarity is in Sec. 3.3 on p.6, not p.5. || The paper writes 'M61' but never spells it out as 2^61-1. The bit width is not stated. || ePrint 2025/535: received Mar 22, 2025; last revised Mar 23, 2025. Tables 1 and 2 were confirmed. No CPU model, verifier time, proof size or soundness statement is given.

technique: Compiles TFLite models into halo2 (Plonkish) ZK-SNARK circuits. It uses gadgets for shape, arithmetic, pointwise non-linearities and specialised ops, plus a cost-model optimizer that picks gadgets and the circuit layout (columns and rows). Backend is KZG or IPA. Values are fixed-point with a scale factor that ZKML chooses.
soundness_error_stated: Not quantified. Sec 4.3 (p.5) says 'ZKML inherits all of the assumptions and security properties of the underlying proving system', i.e. halo2 knowledge soundness and zero-knowledge. No bit-security figure is given.
trust_assumptions: KZG needs a one-time universal trusted setup. The paper uses the Privacy Scaling Explorations ceremony for 2^28 (>75 participants, p.5). IPA needs no trusted setup and 'usually' has larger proofs and slower verification. The weights are private (knowledge soundness means the prover knows the input and weights).
handles_nonlinear: Pointwise non-linearities (ReLU, exp and others) use lookup tables. Bit decomposition over arithmetic rows is an alternative the optimizer weighs (Sec 3 toy example, 16-bit ReLU). Max uses lookups, and variable division and scaled exponentiation have their own gadgets. Softmax and BatchMatMul are supported (Table 3).
weights_public: Only partially. The repo's examples/ has mnist (model.tflite plus msgpack files, public), nlp, train_graph, twitter and v2_1.0_224_truncated. The ResNet-18/VGG-16 CIFAR-10 weights are not confirmed in the repo. 7 of ZKML's 8 models (mnist, resnet, dlrm, mobilenet, vgg, gpt2, diffusion; Twitter excluded) are distributed as msgpack (360MB) by the Artemis authors: 'aws s3 sync s3://pps-artemis-artifacts/models examples/models' (github.com/pps-lab/artemis README; the README does not say whether AWS credentials are needed). None are gated.
verifier_corrections: All numbers in Tables 5-12 and 14 were re-checked against the EuroSys'24 PDF (ddkang.github.io) and match, including units, page numbers and hardware. Tables 5 and 6-8 are on pp.10-11, Tables 9-10 on p.12, Tables 11-14 on p.13, the Sec 4.3 security text and the '2^28 ... over 75 participants' ceremony on p.5, and the hardware on p.11. || weights_public: ZKML evaluates 8 models. The zkml repo's examples/ also has a train_graph folder, and examples/mnist has model.msgpack/converted_model.msgpack alongside model.tflite. || Table 9 hardware: the sentence 'we match the hardware setup used in the prior work as closely as possible' is about estimating the cost of prior work. technique: Compiles ONNX models, via a transpiler and graph-rewriting compiler, into a DAG of 'basic blocks' such as CQ/CQLin lookups, matmul and additions. Each block is proved with a specialised KZG-based Poly-IOP, and the many per-block proofs are folded with a parallel extension of the Mira pairing-based accumulation scheme. It runs over BN254 and supports 61 layer types.
soundness_error_stated: Union bound over DAG nodes. 'we have at most 100,000 nodes in our DAG, so we can achieve a total soundness error of e by setting the threshold of each individual node at 1/(10^6) e'. The paper adds that 'due to our field size, this error is negligible' (Sec 4.3, p.6). Knowledge soundness is argued in the AGM (Appendix B/C).
trust_assumptions: KZG polynomial commitments on the pairing-friendly curve BN254 over a 254-bit prime field, which needs an SRS. Security is argued in the AGM with Fiat-Shamir. The weights stay hidden from the verifier.
handles_nonlinear: Lookup basic blocks (CQ). For example, GeLU (4 Mul, 1 Pow, 1 Tanh in ONNX) is fused into one CQ lookup, and nonlinearities are combined wherever possible (Sec 5). Rescaling after CQLin uses CQ.

technique: A PyTorch-to-ONNX preprocessor builds a DAG with extra auxiliary nodes (for example, a division remainder). ZKP-friendly static quantisation brings values into small fields such as M61. A hierarchical optimizer works at three levels: model level (batch proving of LLM tokens or CNN images), primitive-operation level (it integrates known techniques such as zkCNN-style FFT convolution and zkLLM-style lookups) and circuit level (parallel sub-circuits). The circuits are proved with Polyhedra's Expander (GKR-based) engine.
soundness_error_stated: Not stated in paper.
trust_assumptions: Not stated in the paper. It depends on the Expander backend.

technique: Sum-check PIOPs (layer-by-layer, GKR-like) plus logup-GKR lookup arguments, with batching across tokens. It certifies the output sequence by running inference on the concatenated input and output tokens, rather than emulating the KV cache in-circuit. There are two PCS options: BaseFold over the Goldilocks field (Ceno library, 'plausible post-quantum') or HyperKZG over BN254 (shorter proofs). A distributed prover partitions the layers into chunks.
soundness_error_stated: No numeric bound in the main text. 'We formally prove that each component is round-by-round (knowledge) sound', which the authors use to argue soundness after the Fiat-Shamir transformation (Sec 1.2; proofs in the appendices).
trust_assumptions: BaseFold is transparent and hash-based over Goldilocks. HyperKZG needs a pairing SRS over BN254. Fiat-Shamir is used in the non-interactive variant.
handles_nonlinear: Lookup arguments (Logup GKR) for activations, Softmax and requantisation. It has specialised PIOPs for LayerNorm and RMSNorm that avoid in-circuit square roots and inverses, plus multi-head/grouped-query attention and RoPE. Activations are clamped, and residuals use mixed precision.

venue_year: IACR ePrint 2026/1112 (received 30 May 2026); ePrint lists 'Published elsewhere. Minor revision. CCS 2026'
technique: Sum-check PIOPs (layer-by-layer, GKR-like) plus logup-GKR lookup arguments, with batching across tokens. It certifies the output sequence by running inference on the concatenated input and output tokens, rather than emulating the KV cache in-circuit. There are two PCS options: BaseFold over the Goldilocks field (Ceno library, 'plausible post-quantum') or HyperKZG over BN254 (shorter proofs). A distributed prover partitions the layers into chunks.
soundness_error_stated: No numeric bound in the main text. 'We formally prove that each component is round-by-round (knowledge) sound', which the authors use to argue soundness after the Fiat-Shamir transformation (Sec 1.2; proofs in the appendices).
trust_assumptions: BaseFold is transparent and hash-based over Goldilocks. HyperKZG needs a pairing SRS over BN254. Fiat-Shamir is used in the non-interactive variant.
handles_nonlinear: Lookup arguments (Logup GKR) for activations, Softmax and requantisation. It has specialised PIOPs for LayerNorm and RMSNorm that avoid in-circuit square roots and inverses, plus multi-head/grouped-query attention and RoPE. Activations are clamped, and residuals use mixed precision.

system: Artemis (extra: commit-and-prove SNARK on the ZKML model zoo)
technique: A CP-SNARK that binds a halo2/ZKML inference proof to an external homomorphic polynomial commitment to the weights. The committed polynomial is evaluated at a verifier challenge inside the circuit using Horner's method, via halo2's Challenge API. It works with KZG (BN254) or IPA (Pallas, no trusted setup). Baselines are No Commitment (plain ZKML arithmetization), Poseidon hashing in-circuit, Lunar CPlink, and Apollo, the authors' improved Lunar.
soundness_error_stated: Knowledge soundness error 'negligible in the security parameter' (appendix proofs). No numeric bit level stated.
trust_assumptions: KZG over BN254 needs an SRS; IPA over Pallas is transparent. The Poseidon baseline switches to BLS12-381 for Diffusion and GPT-2 because it needs more rows than BN254 allows.
handles_nonlinear: Reuses ZKML's arithmetization (lookups).
weights_public: 7 ZKML models (mnist, resnet, dlrm, mobilenet, vgg, gpt2, diffusion) as msgpack files (360MB) in a public S3 bucket: 'aws s3 sync s3://pps-artemis-artifacts/models examples/models'. Setup params are params_kzg (64GB) and params_ipa (15GB). The README does not say whether AWS credentials are needed. None are gated.
verifier_corrections: All 14 Table 1 (p.15) Artemis cells (proof kB, verifier ms, prover memory GB) and the No-Commitment baselines were re-checked and match. So do the instances (Sec 5.2, p.14: VGG-16 and GPT-2 on r6i.32xlarge, Diffusion on x2idn.metal), the overhead ranges, the abstract's '11.5x to 1.1x', the >4096GB Poseidon failure, BN254/Pallas and the BLS12-381 Poseidon switch. || The snippets were paraphrased. I replaced them with the verbatim Table 1 row strings and noted the relevant column.
other_costs: Prover memory 0.60 GB. No-Commitment baseline: 9 kB / 7 ms / 0.53 GB.

venue_year: Technical report, arXiv 2025 (arXiv:2510.06784v2, 8 Dec 2025), Rarimo / Distributed Lab
technique: R1CS (Circom) circuits proved with Groth16 or the authors' UltraGroth, a Groth16 variant with lookup tables. The weights are treated as circuit constants rather than witness signals, so multiplication by weights is essentially free. It uses a custom Rapidsnark fork and targets on-device (mobile) proving and EVM verification. Its Table 4 compares against EZKL, ZKML and zkCNN on the same machine, with deep-prove only in Figure 6.
soundness_error_stated: UltraGroth is proven complete, sound and zero-knowledge in the generic group model and random oracle model (Appendix A). The lookup inclusion check has soundness error up to (n+d)/|F| (Sec 5.3). The field is BN254. No overall bit-security figure is given in the benchmark section.
trust_assumptions: Groth16-style circuit-specific trusted setup. The weights must be public: 'we do not support private model weights'.
handles_nonlinear: In plain R1CS, ReLU uses bit decomposition: 'The ReLU and LeakyReLU activations can be implemented in R1CS with b + 1 constraints', and a precision cut after ReLU is free. UltraGroth adds lookup tables (a logUp-style inclusion check following [Hab22]) for range checks with limbs, which the authors say significantly reduced the overhead of non-linear layers.
code_url: Not public. Sec 7 (Conclusion) says 'we plan to make the Bionetta framework open-sourced'.
weights_public: The benchmark models (MNIST MLP, LeNet5, VGG11-mini, ResNet18, MobileNetV2) are not released.
verifier_corrections: handles_nonlinear: 'No lookups' is WRONG. Sec 5 is titled 'UltraGroth: Lookup Tables in R1CS'. UltraGroth 'enables lookup tables in Groth16 with the tiny verification overhead', using a logUp-style inclusion check following [Hab22] for range checks. The b+1-constraint bit-decomposition ReLU and the free precision cut are the plain-R1CS parts. || soundness_error: the paper does state some bounds. The lookup inclusion check has 'soundness error of up to (n+d)/|F|' (Sec 5.3), and a theorem says UltraGroth is complete, sound and zero-knowledge in the GGM and ROM (proof in Appendix A). || notes: 'MobileNetV2 uses 28x28 inputs' is not stated for the benchmark. 28x28 appears only in the Table 1 capability criterion ('28x28 MobileNetV2 can be proven in less than 30 seconds...'). Sec 6.1 gives an input size (flattened 28x28) only for the MNIST model. || technique: Table 4 compares only Bionetta+UltraGroth, ezkl, zkml and zkCNN. Footnote 7 excludes keras2circom and deep-prove from the table, and deep-prove appears only in Figure 6. || All Table 4 (p.25) values were re-checked by word-coordinate extraction and match, including PK, VK and RAM. The hardware (Sec 6.1, p.23), '270 seconds down to only 15', the iPhone 14 Pro 23 s/14 s figures (Table 6: 22.96/13.60 s) and eps_15 ≈ 5.2·10^-3 also match. arXiv v2 is dated 8 Dec 2025.
other_costs: RAM 0.27 GB; PK 0.20 GB; VK 0.004 MB

system: Jolt Atlas (extra: 2026 lookup-based zkML over ONNX)
technique: Adapts Jolt's lookup-centric sum-check approach from CPU instructions to ONNX tensor operations: no registers or general RAM, just a tensor trace. It uses prefix-suffix decomposed lookup tables, a HyperKZG PCS, a streaming prover and 'neural teleportation' (adapted from TeleSparse), with zero-knowledge from BlindFold (Nova-style folding).
soundness_error_stated: Not stated numerically.
trust_assumptions: HyperKZG, a pairing-based PCS that needs an SRS. ZK comes from BlindFold. Future work proposes lattice PCS for post-quantum security.
handles_nonlinear: Lookup arguments with decomposable tables; for example, the input is split into C segments of b bits (e.g. C = 8 segments of b = 8 bits).
code_url: https://github.com/ICME-Lab/jolt-atlas (public repo found via web search; not cited in the paper)
weights_public: nanoGPT is EZKL's model. GPT-2 (125M) is OpenAI's public model, ungated.

technique: Interactive zero-knowledge proof built on sumchecks over multilinear extensions for tensor operations (zkCNN/GKR-style matmul sumchecks; zkGPT notes zkLLM adopts the matmul protocol of its ref [56]). Tensors and weights are committed with Hyrax, a Pedersen-commitment variant, on BLS12-381. 'tlookup' is a parallel lookup argument for non-arithmetic tensor ops. 'zkAttn' proves softmax/attention via segmented exponent lookups. The prover is CUDA on GPU (ec-gpu BLS12-381 code). The sequential verifier parts are adapted from zkCNN and the mcl library (p.11).
soundness_error_stated: Stated only as negligible in λ (Thm 7.3 for tlookup, plus sumcheck and Pedersen/Hyrax proof-of-opening soundness, p.10). The tlookup proof sketch loses O(D/|F|) and O(ND/|F|) terms. The implementation uses BLS12-381 with '|F| ≈ 2^254' (p.10). Completeness error: honest-prover failure is 'at most O(C/|F|)', with C = total size of tensors in non-arithmetic ops (p.10). The paper assumes 'a commitment scheme that ensures λ-bit security' and |F| = Ω(2^{2λ}) (p.5). No concrete bit-security figure is given.
trust_assumptions: Hyrax/Pedersen commitments (discrete log), so no trusted setup (p.4). The protocol is interactive: the verifier sends random challenges in Protocol 1, and the paper does not use Fiat-Shamir. The verifier is assumed semi-honest: it reports accept/reject accurately but tries to learn the weights (p.5). There is a one-time weight-commitment phase ('Committing time' in Table 1).
handles_nonlinear: Yes. Activations and rescaling use tlookup, with each tlookup of size 2^16. Softmax in zkAttn uses K=5 tlookups of size 2^16, of which L=3 are least-significant segments (paper's notation, p.11). The paper reports an approximate total L1 output error of 10^-2 (p.11).
weights_public: Llama-2-7B/13B are gated. The README requires logging in to Hugging Face, sharing contact info on the model pages, and a read access token. OPT-125M to OPT-13B (facebook/opt-*) and C4 download from Hugging Face without an account (general knowledge, not stated in the paper). The repo (MIT licence, archived Jul 10 2025) only scripts meta-llama/Llama-2-7b-hf and Llama-2-13b-hf; its README does not mention OPT. It was tested on A6000 and A40, recommends CUDA 12.1.0, and is GPU-only.
verifier_corrections: All Table 1 numbers (p.12) re-checked against the arXiv 2404.16109 PDF for all 8 models: committing time, commitment size, prover time, proof size, verifier time, memory, and C4 perplexity orig/quant. All match. The hardware (p.11) matches too; the paper itself writes the GPU as 'A100SMX4', a typo. || The paper's notation is 'L = 3 least significant segments' (p.11), not 'M=3'. In Thm 7.1, M is a different segment count. || The semi-honest verifier and the 'λ-bit security' commitment assumption are on p.5, not p.4. p.4 is where Hyrax is introduced (a Pedersen variant with no trusted setup, based on DLog). || Complexity, zkAttn: the paper (Sec 7.3.2, p.11) gives communication and verifier cost as O(K·√(mn)), not O(K log N). Prover and memory cost are O(K·mn). || 'GPT-2 (1.5B parameters)' is stated in the body text on p.12 that accompanies Fig. 4. technique: Non-interactive ZK proof built on GKR/sumcheck, based on the zkCNN code. It uses the Hyrax polynomial commitment on BN254 and is made non-interactive with Fiat-Shamir. The matmul sumcheck is optimised (grouping, exploiting small quantised value ranges and padded zeros, precomputed multiplications). Non-linear layers are proven from prover-supplied advice checked with Lasso lookups (range and exponentiation relations). Two further optimisations are 'constraint fusion' (merging adjacent rounding constraints) and 'circuit squeeze' (breaking layer dependency via committed advice to increase parallelism). Runs on CPU (C++, mcl library).
soundness_error_stated: App. B: in Case 1, via Schwartz-Zippel, the check fails to catch an error with probability at most 1/|F|. The Lasso checks pass with probability at most O((m1 + N1^{1/c} + m2 + N2)/|F|), stated as 'negligible'. The overall union bound is stated only as negligible. Implementation: 'BN254 provides around 100 bits of security' (Sec 7.1, p.2055).
trust_assumptions: Hyrax PCS, which is transparent (no trusted setup). Discrete log on BN254; Fiat-Shamir (random oracle). The prover range-proves committed quantised weights in [0, 2^Q], and the quantised input embedding is public.
handles_nonlinear: Yes. GeLU, Softmax and LayerNorm are proven via advice plus range/exponentiation lookup relations (Lasso). Constraint fusion reduces GeLU rounding constraints from 2sd to sd and normalisation rounding constraints from 3s+2sd to s+sd, each 'nearly 50%' (PDF p.11).

technique: General-purpose ZKML compiler. ONNX graphs are transpiled into a DAG of 'basic blocks': 20 are listed in Table 1, 13 of them foldable, and together they cover 61 ML layers. Each block is proved by a specialised KZG-based protocol, e.g. CQ/CQ2 lookups, CQLin/MatMul, and a Poly-IOP for the rest. A parallelised extension of the Mira accumulation scheme folds repeated basic blocks into one succinct proof. BN254 curve; CPU prover (arkworks).
soundness_error_stated: All protocols are complete and knowledge sound. DAG soundness follows from a union bound: with at most 100,000 nodes, a total error e is reached by setting each node's threshold at e/10^6, and 'due to our field size, this error is negligible' (p.6). BN254 has a 254-bit prime field (p.11).
trust_assumptions: KZG commitments with a structured reference string from a powers-of-tau ceremony (universal trusted setup; secure if one party is honest). SDH assumption; algebraic group model; Fiat-Shamir (p.2).
handles_nonlinear: Yes, via lookup basic blocks (CQ for set inclusion, CQ2 for lookup tables). GeLU's 4 Mul, 1 Pow and 1 Tanh are fused into one CQ (p.10-11). Softmax is composed to prioritise accuracy (p.9). Graph-transformation rules cover GeLU, MultiHeadMatMul and RoPE (p.10). ReLU is a supported layer but not a Table 1 basic block.

technique: Compiler from PyTorch to ONNX to a DAG, then to circuits for the Expander GKR-based prover (Polyhedra). A ZKP-friendly static quantisation module (symmetric per-tensor) fits computations into small fields such as M61. Lookup tables handle non-linear ops. A hierarchical optimiser works at three levels: model level (batch verification of all LLM tokens in one circuit), primitive-operation level (reusing techniques from zkCNN/zkLLM) and circuit level (parallel sub-circuits).
soundness_error_stated: Not stated in the paper. The field is M61; the paper does not say whether an extension field is used for challenges.
trust_assumptions: Not stated in the paper. It inherits the assumptions of the Expander GKR prover.
handles_nonlinear: Yes. Lookup constraints cover ReLU, softmax and normalisation, with auxiliary witnesses (e.g. division remainders plus a proof that the remainder is smaller than the divisor; range proofs). Softmax exp and RMSNorm sqrt use temporary bit-width adjustments and piecewise lookup tables (p.6).

technique: Adapts the Jolt lookup-centric sumcheck prover to ONNX tensor operations. Per the abstract, unlike zkVMs it does not emulate CPU instructions, although Sec 5.4 describes a CPU-trace path being replaced by tensor-level checks. It uses the HyperKZG polynomial commitment. Zero knowledge comes from BlindFold: the sumcheck verifier is encoded as R1CS and folded Nova-style with a random instance. 'Neural teleportation' shrinks lookup tables. The prover is streaming (memory-constrained), using prefix-suffix decomposition.
soundness_error_stated: Not stated.
trust_assumptions: Pairing-based HyperKZG PCS; that it requires an SRS is general knowledge and not stated in the paper. The paper lists lattice PCS as future work for post-quantum security. Fiat-Shamir challenges are used.
handles_nonlinear: Yes, via decomposable lookup arguments (e.g. ReLU from the sign bit, p.15). With teleportation factor τ=4, the lookup table is 'bounded by 2^16 entries (sufficient for 16-bit fixed-point activations)' (p.16).

technique: Linear layers are proved with specialised sum-check PIOPs, composed GKR-style. Non-linear layers and requantisation use LogUp-GKR lookup arguments over decomposable tables, with operator fusion (delayed requantisation). The prover commits only to model parameters and lookup witnesses. It certifies the full output sequence (all generated tokens) and is made non-interactive via Fiat-Shamir, with round-by-round soundness. It is implemented in Rust on Scroll's Ceno library (Goldilocks field), with two PCS options: BaseFold, or HyperKZG on BN254. It also has a distributed (chunked) prover and an optional proof-of-non-hallucination module.
soundness_error_stated: Each PIOP is proved round-by-round (knowledge) sound. For example, the batched MatMul PIOP has rbr error max(h(1+2 log max(n_i)max(m_i))/|F|, ε_sum) (appendix, p.20). The implementation uses the 64-bit Goldilocks base field, or BN254 for HyperKZG. This check did not locate an extension field for challenges or an end-to-end concrete bit-security figure.
trust_assumptions: BaseFold version: hash-based, described as 'plausible post-quantum secure' (p.10). HyperKZG version: pairing-based on BN254, with shorter proofs; that it needs an SRS is general knowledge. Non-interactive via Fiat-Shamir. No input privacy (per Maverick).
handles_nonlinear: Yes. Softmax, GeLU, LayerNorm, RMSNorm and requantisation use LogUp-GKR lookups over decomposable tables (pp.4-8). Over 50% of prover cost comes from activations, Softmax and requantisation (p.11).
